The validated edge here is the absolute-trend gate (gate_helps=true), which is doing its job: 8 of 16 themes eligible, the rest gated out. Without those two conditions, no handoff is confirmed.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners (rank 2, eligible, uncrowded) is the one leg that combines trend-gate eligibility with the cleanest crowding profile among the top ranks. Oil & Gas leads but is crowded (z=1.04); Gold's crowding_z is 0.2, so a trend-following lean here doesn't fight the reflexivity problem. Durability (0.48) is weaker than the leader's, and breadth (0.267) is narrow, so this is durability-uncertain — but the absolute-trend gate supports staying-power risk control, and rotation margin (0.502) is wide enough that a challenger lean is not a fade call.
evidence: rank=2 challenger behind Oil & Gas, margin 0.502
durability_bar=0.48 with hurst_tag=mixed (no confirmed trend persistence)
theses.dissent: Breadth is only 0.267 — this is a narrow, non-cohesive move. Hurst_tag is mixed, meaning the trend isn't persistent; a mean-reversion snap-back is plausible. Gold's theme momentum rank has no forward edge anyway.

theses.subject: Oil & Gas Producers
theses.thesis: Oil & Gas is the dominant leader (rank 1, score 1.61, durability 0.68, breadth 0.786) but is crowded (z=1.04). Per guardrails, crowding is a size-down caution, NOT a fade — but with the leader already crowded and dir_accuracy at 0.343, chasing the leader is a low-conviction proposition. The trend-gate supports it (eligible), and breadth/cohesion are the best in the board, so this is a durability-positive story. Lean is 'avoid' as a caution flag, not a fade.
theses.dissent: This is the strongest trend on the board with the best breadth and durability. Avoiding it could mean missing the one real directional leg. Oil & Gas in Canada often has fundamental tailwinds (energy demand, dividend yield) the detector can't see.

falsifier.text: XEG.TO maintains trend-gate eligibility AND crowding_z stays below 1.0 for 15 consecutive trading days

theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Big Banks (rank 5, eligible, uncrowded, hurst_tag=trend) is the only theme in the board with a clean 'trend' Hurst tag AND trend-gate eligibility AND no crowding flag. Durability_bar (0.59) is second only to Oil & Gas, breadth (0.143) is narrow but trend-tag suggests persistence. In a market where the only validated edge is trend-gate risk control, a low-conviction lean on the one cleanly-trending eligible theme is the most defensible non-leader call.
evidence: hurst_tag=trend (only top-half theme with clean trend persistence)
theses.dissent: Breadth is only 0.143 — almost no internal confirmation. Rank 5 means the momentum focus lens isn't on banks; this is a contrarian lean on a theme the board doesn't find interesting. Hurst_tag=trend is a coincident texture, not a forward edge.
